research_scope: Independent Wave2 source-free review of shared mathematical prerequisites with original context and non-merge restrictions.

aliases.reason: Both congruence-modulo-m variants for integers use m|(a−b), or existence of k∈ℤ with a−b=km; one emphasizes m>0 and the other m≠0. The common prerequisite is integer divisibility; positive-modulus convention stays parent-specific.

Locally uniform convergence and local quasi-compactness both quantify over general neighborhoods containing an open neighborhood of x, which need not themselves be open. Their respective uniformity and compactness conditions remain parent-level; do not merge these neighborhoods with the stricter open-neighborhood identity.

The constructible-spectrum formulation uses the distinguished open D(f)={p:f∉p}, just as the Zariski-scheme topology and local complete-intersection formulations. These are the same principal Zariski-open prerequisite, with constructible Boolean operations and covering conditions retained in parents.

Local section gluing over standard D(f_i) and the Zariski-topology definition use the same distinguished prime-spectrum open D(f), where f_i is a specialized generator. Pairwise intersections D(f_i f_j), unit-ideal cover and gluing are additional parent conditions.

Scheme morphisms and morphisms of locally ringed spaces require the same local-homomorphism condition on stalk maps O_{Y,f(x)}→O_{X,x}, preserving maximal ideals by inverse image. Scheme-specific global sheaf compatibility is a separate parent condition.
